source_text: Privacy and data-protection baseline
blocker: Unmapped source clause; semantic decomposition and behavioural evidence pending

source_text: 9to1 MUST apply a platform-wide Privacy Ceiling baseline to every app, framework, cloud service, hosted component, telemetry path, AI feature and operating-system integration that processes personal information. Product teams MUST NOT treat privacy as an app-specific optional enhancement.
blocker: Unmapped source clause; semantic decomposition and behavioural evidence pending

source_text: The Privacy Ceiling is derived from the strongest compatible protection required across the supported United States jurisdictions, the United Kingdom and the European Union/EEA, plus deliberate engineering headroom. The implementation MUST maintain a versioned LegalPrivacyProfile describing the currently applicable statutory/regulatory requirements for each supported jurisdiction. Where multiple requirements are compatible, the most protective requirement becomes the global default. Where applicable laws genuinely conflict, the exception MUST be narrowly jurisdiction-scoped, documented, legally reviewed and MUST NOT lower protection for unaffected users or data.
blocker: Unmapped source clause; semantic decomposition and behavioural evidence pending

source_text: Engineering headroom means 9to1 SHOULD collect less data, retain it for less time, expose it to fewer systems, process it locally more often and encrypt it more comprehensively than the minimum legally permissible where doing so does not prevent the requested product function. A legal maximum retention period, collection scope or disclosure permission MUST NOT automatically become the product default.
blocker: Unmapped source clause; semantic decomposition and behavioural evidence pending

source_text: Privacy by design and by default is mandatory throughout the product lifecycle. Every processing activity MUST have a declared purpose, lawful/authorised basis where required, data categories, data subjects, recipients/processors, locality/residency constraints where applicable, retention/deletion policy, access-control model and security classification. New processing purposes MUST NOT silently reuse personal data collected for an unrelated purpose merely because the data is technically available.
blocker: Unmapped source clause; semantic decomposition and behavioural evidence pending

source_text: Data minimisation is mandatory. A component MUST request, collect, transmit, persist and expose only the personal data necessary for its declared purpose and current authorised scope. Optional analytics, diagnostics, personalisation, AI context and convenience features MUST NOT enlarge the mandatory data footprint of the core product without a separate valid basis and user/admin control where required.
blocker: Unmapped source clause; semantic decomposition and behavioural evidence pending

source_text: Privacy-protective defaults MUST be the ordinary out-of-box state. Settings that materially broaden sharing, retention, discoverability, telemetry, cloud processing, contactability or third-party disclosure MUST be explicit and understandable. Consent or approval surfaces MUST NOT use dark patterns, misleading symmetry, preselected optional consent or unnecessarily difficult withdrawal.
blocker: Unmapped source clause; semantic decomposition and behavioural evidence pending

source_text: High-risk processing MUST undergo an appropriate documented privacy/risk assessment before release and again after material architectural or purpose changes. The assessment MUST address foreseeable misuse, unauthorised disclosure, inference risk, vulnerable users, children where relevant, cross-border processing, AI/model exposure, account compromise, metadata leakage and recovery/incident handling.
blocker: Unmapped source clause; semantic decomposition and behavioural evidence pending

source_text: Encryption MUST be applied in transit and at rest for sensitive personal information unless a documented technical reason makes a specific layer impossible. Where the product promises end-to-end encryption, only intended endpoint participants may possess the content-decryption capability under the declared trust model. A server-side copy of a universal decryption key, silent escrow path or moderation backdoor is incompatible with an E2EE claim unless the user-facing product explicitly describes a materially different encryption model.
blocker: Unmapped source clause; semantic decomposition and behavioural evidence pending

source_text: E2EE protects content but does not automatically hide all metadata. 9to1 MUST separately minimise and protect metadata such as participant identifiers, relationship graphs, IP/network information, timestamps, device identifiers, routing information and notification data. User interfaces and documentation MUST NOT imply that metadata is cryptographically hidden when the transport/service necessarily observes it.
blocker: Unmapped source clause; semantic decomposition and behavioural evidence pending

source_text: Local processing is preferred for sensitive transformations when it can satisfy the feature reliably. A local application being able to decrypt or access data does NOT automatically grant Dulche, a Plugin, a cloud model, telemetry or another subsystem access to that data. AI access is a separate capability decision subject to the normal permission/privacy model.
blocker: Unmapped source clause; semantic decomposition and behavioural evidence pending

source_text: When a feature can use either a local or cloud model/service, the privacy boundary MUST be explicit. Private content MUST NOT leave the device merely because a cloud provider is configured as a model fallback. Uploading personal content to a cloud model/service requires an applicable authorised route, and the UI MUST make materially relevant remote processing understandable to the user.
blocker: Unmapped source clause; semantic decomposition and behavioural evidence pending

source_text: Secrets, authentication tokens, cryptographic keys and recovery material MUST use dedicated secure storage and least-privilege access. Logs, crash reports, analytics and Action Graph/FullLog data MUST redact secrets and unnecessary personal content rather than creating secondary plaintext stores.
blocker: Unmapped source clause; semantic decomposition and behavioural evidence pending

source_text: Retention MUST be purpose-bound and enforceable. Personal data MUST have a defined deletion/expiry policy or a documented reason for durable retention. Deletion MUST propagate to replicas, caches, indexes and derived stores according to their declared lifecycle rather than only hiding the primary UI record. Legally required preservation or an explicitly created safety/evidence record MUST be segregated from ordinary user-visible retention and governed by its own scope and expiry rules.
blocker: Unmapped source clause; semantic decomposition and behavioural evidence pending

source_text: Users MUST receive the applicable rights and controls required by the active LegalPrivacyProfile, including access/export, correction, deletion, objection/restriction and consent withdrawal where applicable. These controls SHOULD be easier and more complete than the legal minimum when technically reasonable. Export MUST use interoperable formats where practical and MUST NOT require the user to manually reconstruct data from screenshots or unrelated pages.

source_text: 9to1 MUST maintain an inspectable data-flow inventory and processor/subprocessor register for hosted services. Third parties receive only the scopes/data required for their declared role. A provider's terms permitting additional processing do not by themselves authorise 9to1 to send data for that additional purpose.

source_text: Telemetry and product analytics MUST be purpose-limited, minimised and separated from message/document content unless that content is genuinely required for a specifically disclosed diagnostic purpose. Sensitive content MUST NOT be collected merely to improve general analytics. Privacy-preserving aggregation/pseudonymisation SHOULD be used where it meaningfully reduces risk.

source_text: Children and other protected/vulnerable-user contexts MUST receive any higher protection required by the applicable LegalPrivacyProfile. source_text: Security/privacy failures MUST fail closed where continuing would expose personal content or silently weaken a promised protection. If an encryption, permission, privacy-relay or policy control required for a sensitive operation is unavailable, the operation MUST stop or visibly degrade to a clearly described lower-protection mode only when the user is allowed to choose that mode.

source_text: 9to1 Home is the central permission broker for app APIs. A caller never dispatches a protected action directly to the target app without Home first resolving its permission state. If Home is not open, 9to1 opens it and shows the approval prompt before the target action executes. A caller may submit the request to the broker, but the requested app action remains PendingApproval until Home grants it.

source_text: The prompt MUST identify the requesting app/script/MCP, verified caller identity/origin when available, target 9to1 app, requested action names/scopes, elevated/destructive risk and affected object identifiers/counts whenever they can be determined before execution. If impact cannot be determined safely before execution, the prompt MUST display that impact as unknown rather than omit it. Generic wording such as “allow access” is insufficient for scoped or powerful actions.

source_text: Permission requests MAY group actions only when they share the same caller identity, target trust boundary and compatible risk level, and the prompt exposes the complete grouped scope before approval. A grant covers only the exact actions/scopes shown or already trusted. Adding a new action, target scope or higher risk level requires a new approval decision.

source_text: Accept and Trust approves the requested ordinary action scopes and trusts that caller for 30 days. The selected donor revision and applicable licensing obligations MUST be recorded in the donor-parity manifest before implementation.

source_text: 9to1 Play is the structured Agent-game framework and user-facing game surface where humans and Dulche Agents participate as contestants under explicit game rules. Play supports human-vs-Agent, Agent-vs-Agent, mixed teams and spectator-only matches. It is distinct from the built-in Experiences Space: Play owns formal games with contestant slots, rules, typed actions, visibility, turns/rounds, judging/scoring and winner conditions; Experiences owns open-ended conversational roleplay/simulation/story state.

source_text: The canonical reference experience is a generated maths quiz in which the user competes against ten AI Agent contestants. Each contestant receives the same authorised question state, submits independently, cannot see competitors' answers before reveal, and is scored by the game engine using deterministic maths validation where possible.

source_text: 9-1 Planner is the CUI calendar, schedule, countdown and assignment-planning app. It answers when something happens, when something is due, what the user needs to do, and which canonical 9to1 entities are connected to that plan. Planner is not Home Events, which is an ecosystem activity/history timeline; it is not Spaces Tasks, which represent goal-oriented agentic work/runs; and it is not Automations, which own recurring/event/condition-triggered execution.

source_text: Persistent Memory is a core Dulche Den subsystem for durable cross-session information about the user, recurring entities, preferences, decisions, projects and other scoped context that Dulche should be able to retrieve in future conversations or authorised surfaces.
